scope: Retain authored later-content ground quests and their level/tier reward table while removing the NGE player-level-derived quest XP cap; PRE-CU XP-type pools and their existing skill-specific limits remain authoritative. Close the complete OnQuestReceivedReward, OnQuestCompleted, and OnQuestCleared callback inventories and prove that their production listeners preserve authored quest content without introducing player level, profession, expertise, roadmap, or skill-template authority.

findings: Publish 14.1 progression is skill-box and XP-pool based, not driven by an NGE player level table.
The retained quest_experience table is authored quest content keyed by quest level and reward tier and is preserved.
The removed helper converted hidden player difficulty back into player_level.iff xp_required rows and capped every quest reward to half of that NGE level delta.
All retained ground-quest XP routes already enter the PRE-CU combat, crafting, social, or explicit XP grant adapters.
The shared XP grant and native PlayerObject grantExperiencePoints path enforce the receiving XP pool's skill-derived experience limit.

The complete Java source tree contains exactly one OnQuestReceivedReward callback. It reads authored quest content, dispatches it through the authenticated ground-quest reward adapter, and records metrics through the PRE-CU skill-difficulty adapter without mutating player level, profession, expertise, or skill template.

The complete Java source tree contains three OnQuestCompleted listeners: base-player retained-content sequencing, the Mustafar Obi-Wan monitor, and one dormant test listener. The complete OnQuestCleared family is the sole base-player listener. None owns NGE player progression.
